units.translation: b. But on the ship you pierce: But sail, he says, until you reach the innermost part of the sea. For after Scythia is the end of the sea because the Maeotic lake succeeds it, after which is the Arctic ocean. L

c. But pierce, he says, and sail, that is, until you touch the innermost and farthest sea, clearly until you arrive at the innermost recess of the Euxine Pontus; for there Scythia also ends. And Sarmatia succeeds Scythia, and the Maeotis succeeds the Euxine; the Sarmatians dwell around the Maeotis, and beyond the Sarmatians is the Sarmatian and Arctic ocean. P
399-401a. Cytaean: Colchian; for Cytaea is a city of Colchis. There is also another Cytaea, a city of Europe, with the same name as the Scythian one,

at the entrance of the Euxine; from there it takes its beginning. It is used thus as a proper name, whence they call Medea Cytaean. Amarantian with circumflex accent, as Herodian says in the General Prosody (I 222, 17 L.). Amarantos is a city in Pontus; but as he himself says, the Amaranta are mountains of Colchis, from which the river Phasis flows down. Ignorant of this, Hegestratus of Ephesus rendered Amarantians as meadows of the Phasis because they are flourishing and unfading. That the Amaranta are mountains of the Colchians, Ctesias relates in book 2 (fg 94 M. Herod. rec. Dind. 1844, App. 106). The Phasis flows from the mountains of Armenia, as Eratosthenes says (fg III B 75 Berger), and empties into the sea at Colchis. Circaeum is a place in Colchis, named after Circe, the sister of Aeetes, or a plain. It cannot be named after the other Circe. For there were two Circes, about whom we will speak in what follows. And Timaeus (fg 9 M. I 195) says that there is a plain in Colchis called Circaeum.
b. Circaean: Circaeum is accented on the antepenult. Lg (P)
404-05a. Shady grove: instead of shady. Hellanicus

(4 fg 129 J.) says that the fleece lies in the sanctuary of Zeus. Many mention the so-called Ares' plain in Colchis and the precinct of Ares there. He says that the golden fleece is dedicated in the grove of Ares on a certain oak, guarded by a monstrous dragon in size. Shady instead of shady according to the Ionic addition of the iota.
b. Monster: instead of wonder. Lg
409. Struck with speechlessness: as if struck dumb with amazement. Lg P
413-18a. Gladly from you: gladly would I learn from you, if indeed we shall return from Colchis and escape.
